The counselling window closed at five, and it was already four. Arnab's finger hovered over the branch list on the college portal. Mechanical, electrical, civil: none had ever made his pulse jump. But Arohi and the whole group had ticked electronics, and choosing the same felt safe. He ticked electronics too and pressed submit with three minutes to spare.
Months into the second year, in a circuits class, he found himself watching the clock more than the board. The subjects were explained clearly, but he felt nothing for them. His friends were busy with problem sets they enjoyed, and he copied theirs just to keep up.

"Come on, we'll be in the same hostel, same classes. It'll be like school." Anand had liked biology more than anything, but mechanical felt safe with friends around. He ticked the same box. The first term was fun: shared tiffins, late-night chai, the four of them walking to class together. Then came thermodynamics and machine drawing. Anand sat in lectures doodling cells and leaves in his margins. His friends argued happily about engines. He didn't care about engines. By the second year his marks were sliding, and he'd started reading biology articles at night instead of studying.

qa.q: Which branch did Anand's friends choose?
qa.a: Mechanical engineering, at the same college in Nagpur.

qa.q: How does Anand seem to feel by the second year?
qa.a: He feels bored and disconnected in class, and a little lost, since his real interest is still biology.

qa.q: What else could Anand have done before ticking the same box?
qa.a: Asked himself which subjects he'd enjoy for four years, and talked to a counsellor about biology options.

qa.q: How might Varun see Anand's struggles?
qa.a: Varun may not notice at first, since he enjoys the subjects; once he does, he might feel guilty for pushing Anand to join.

"Yogesh, you're doing civil too, right? All four of us together!"
"I… I guess, Sachin. Everyone is."
"You don't sound sure."
"I'm sure. It's safe. We'll help each other."
Eight months later, in the hostel corridor.
"Yogesh, surveying lab starts in ten minutes."
"I'm not going."
"What? Why?"
"Sachin, I don't like any of it. Soil, concrete, load. I sit there and feel nothing."
"Then why did you pick it?"
"Because you all did. I thought being with friends would be enough."
"What do you actually like?"
Yogesh looked at the floor. "Writing. I used to write stories. I never even checked if there was a course for that."
Sachin sat down next to him, quiet.

qa.q: What does Yogesh say he used to do?
How does Yogesh feel about the civil engineering subjects?
qa.a: He feels flat and unhappy, saying he sits there and feels nothing.
Talk to a college counsellor about his interest in writing and what options exist, rather than just skipping labs.

qa.q: How might Sachin feel hearing this?
qa.a: Sachin seems shocked and sad, sitting quietly, perhaps realising the group's choice didn't suit everyone.

grounding: A student picks the same engineering branch as his friends because it feels safe, and later finds he has little interest in it.
